area: mobile operation - companion dashboard shell, mount/sequencer/log/settings tabs, session picker and session replay, driven disconnected on the ns_test_api35 emulator

units_unreached.why: SessionReplayScreen requires a runId and is pushed from exactly one place, session_picker_screen.dart:244 `builder: (_) => SessionReplayScreen(runId: run.id)`, inside the tap handler of a run row. Run rows come from NetworkBackend.fetchSequenceRuns, so the list is only ever non-empty when the phone is paired with a host that has completed sequence runs in its database. Driven disconnected, the picker correctly renders its 'Connect to a server' empty state instead of any rows, so there is no row to tap and no runId to pass. Pairing with the one appliance reachable from this emulator (another agent's live desktop on the host) would both break the no-appliance premise of this sweep and disturb a concurrent audit. Source-only observations: the screen accepts a dataSourceOverride for tests (session_replay_screen.dart:35-41), and its own disconnected behaviour is therefore untested here.

findings.title: The entire companion dashboard - and with it the only editor for the 10 push-notification toggles - cannot be opened in a shipped release APK
findings.what_happened: MobileDashboardScreen (Devices/Mount/Camera/Sequencer/Science/Log/Settings) mounts only when isCompanionUiEnabled is true. That getter is `bool.fromEnvironment('SKOTIQ_COMPANION_UI')` OR `Platform.environment['SKOTIQ_COMPANION_UI'] == '1'`. The release workflow builds the APK with a bare `flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi` and passes no such dart-define, and Platform.environment on a non-debuggable Android app cannot be set by a user. So in every published build the flag is permanently false and all seven tabs, plus SessionPickerScreen and SessionReplayScreen (whose ONLY constructor call site in the whole repo is mobile_dashboard_screen.dart:168), are unreachable. That is ~6,700 lines of shipped-but-unopenable UI. The sharpest consequence: settings_tab.dart is the only surface anywhere that writes the ten `mobile.notify.*` SharedPreferences keys, and those keys ARE read and enforced at runtime by mobile_event_notifier.dart:162/325 and mobile_sequence_hooks.dart:478. All ten default to true. So a user is permanently opted in to every push category - meridian flip, safety, guiding lost, battery, per-target completed - with no way to mute any of them, and no way to check the setting when a category is not firing.
findings.expected: Either the release build passes --dart-define=SKOTIQ_COMPANION_UI=1, or the notification toggles and session replay are re-hosted on a surface the shared SkotiqApp shell actually routes to. A preference that gates whether the phone pages you at 3am must be user-visible; shipping it enforced-but-uneditable is worse than not shipping it.
findings.repro: 1. `python3 tools/ui_audit/drive_android.py start` on the stock installed APK -> Skip Connection -> bottom nav reads Home/Gear/Imaging/Sequence/Guiding/Plan/More (the shared shell). No Devices/Mount/Camera/Sequencer/Science/Log/Settings tabs exist and there is no route to Session Replay. 2. `adb root; adb shell setprop wrap.com.skotiq.mobile SKOTIQ_COMPANION_UI=1`; restart -> Skip Connection -> the seven companion tabs now appear. The only difference is a process env var that a release build cannot receive.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/lib/companion_ui_config.dart:7-14 (the getter). .github/workflows/release.yml:163 `run: flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi` - grep for 'dart-define' across .github/workflows returns only REQUIRE_MIGRATION_ARTIFACT (ci.yml:213) and SKOTIQ_UPDATE_PUBLIC_KEY for the Windows build (release.yml:398); SKOTIQ_COMPANION_UI appears in no build command. `grep -rn 'SessionPickerScreen\|SessionReplayScreen' --include=*.dart` outside the replay dir returns exactly one call site: mobile_dashboard_screen.dart:168. `grep -rn 'mobilePreferencesProvider' --include=*.dart` outside tests returns only camera_tab.dart:58, settings_tab.dart, and first_run_setup_screen.dart - all three inside the flagged-off dashboard subtree. Consumers that enforce the prefs regardless: apps/mobile/lib/services/mobile_event_notifier.dart:162 `if (!_preferences.notifySafety) return;`, :325 notifyMeridianFlip, apps/mobile/lib/services/mobile_sequence_hooks.dart:478. Defaults, apps/mobile/lib/services/mobile_preferences.dart:81-125: all ten `?? true`. Emulator a11y tree before the wrap prop, after Skip Connection: bottom nav = Home/Gear/Imaging/Sequence/Guiding/Plan/More. After the wrap prop: Devices/Mount/Camera/Sequencer/Science/Log/Settings.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide which shell ships. If the shared shell is the product, move the ten notification toggles and the Session Replay entry point into it (they have no equivalent there today) and delete the companion subtree rather than shipping it dark. If the companion shell is meant to be available, add --dart-define=SKOTIQ_COMPANION_UI=1 behind an in-app developer setting rather than a build flag, so it is switchable on a release device.

findings.title: Sequencer tab shows a red 'Weather safety: Unsafe' alarm on a phone that has never contacted a host and has no weather data
findings.what_happened: With no appliance ever paired, the Sequencer tab's sticky header renders 'Weather safety' with a red alert-triangle pill reading 'Unsafe'. The header is COLLAPSED by default, so the red 'Unsafe' verdict is the only thing the user sees. Expanding the card contradicts it outright: 'SAFETY: Unsafe / Data: Unavailable / Connect to an imaging host to evaluate weather safety.' The app is simultaneously asserting a safety verdict and admitting it has no data to base one on. Root cause is that WeatherSafetyStatus has exactly three members - safe, unsafe, snoozed - with no 'unknown', and WeatherSafetyState.initial() picks unsafe with reason 'Weather safety has not been evaluated yet'. Fail-closed is defensible on the desktop, which is the actor that would refuse to open the roof. It is not defensible on a remote companion that cannot park anything: the phone's only job here is to report, and it is reporting a red alarm about weather it has never sampled.
findings.expected: When dataSource is SafetyDataSource.unavailable the pill should read 'Unknown' or 'No data' in a neutral/secondary colour, never the error colour with an alertTriangle. The collapsed header must carry the qualifier that the expanded card already has - a user who never expands the tile must not be left believing conditions were measured and found unsafe.
findings.repro: 1. adb shell setprop wrap.com.skotiq.mobile SKOTIQ_COMPANION_UI=1; drive_android.py start. 2. Skip Connection (View UI Only) - no host is ever contacted. 3. Bottom nav -> Sequencer (tap-xy 540 2253). 4. Read the header at [0,472][1080,619]. 5. Tap it to expand.
findings.evidence: a11y tree, collapsed (step 4): `View: Weather safety / Unsafe, Collapsed [0,472][1080,619]`. a11y tree, expanded (step 5): `View: SAFETY [144,671][558,716]` / `View: Unsafe [642,674][731,713]` / `View: Data [87,757][146,801]` / `View: Unavailable [823,755][993,803]` / `View: Connect to an imaging host to evaluate weather safety. [163,847][970,892]`. Source: apps/mobile/lib/screens/dashboard/tabs/sequencer_tab.dart:671-683 switches on safety.status over only safe/unsafe/snoozed and maps unsafe -> ('Unsafe', colors.error, LucideIcons.alertTriangle) with no unavailable branch. packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/weather_safety_provider.dart:92-102 defines the three-member enum; :201-214 WeatherSafetyState.initial() sets status: WeatherSafetyStatus.unsafe, dataSource: SafetyDataSource.unavailable, reason: 'Weather safety has not been evaluated yet'.
findings.proposed_fix: Add WeatherSafetyStatus.unknown (or derive it in the view from dataSource == SafetyDataSource.unavailable) and render it as ('Unknown', colors.textSecondary, LucideIcons.helpCircle). Keep the fail-closed behaviour for the desktop's actuation path - a phone label and a run-gating decision are different questions and should not share one enum value.

findings.title: Log severity filter chips expose no on/off state to accessibility - TalkBack announces an active and a muted filter identically
findings.what_happened: The Log tab's four severity filters (Info/Warning/Error/Critical) are built as a bare InkWell + Container. Selection is expressed only through the container decoration and the label colour; the widget wraps nothing in Semantics and sets no selected/toggled flag. Toggling a chip therefore produces ZERO change in the accessibility tree. I tapped the Error chip and the uiautomator dump was byte-identical before and after - `View: Error [477,304][667,419]` both times - even though a screenshot confirms the chip really did flip from filled-red to grey-outline. The app already proves it knows how to do this properly elsewhere: the Settings switches dump as `[ON]`/`[off]` and the shared shell dumps `Switch: Glance mode [off]`. A TalkBack user cannot determine which severities are currently being hidden, which on this screen means they cannot tell whether an empty log means 'nothing happened' or 'you filtered it out'.
findings.expected: Wrap each chip in `Semantics(selected: enabled, button: true, label: '<severity>, N events')` (or use a real FilterChip, which does this for free) so the state is announced and appears in the tree as ON/off like every other toggle in the app.
findings.repro: 1. Companion UI enabled; Skip Connection. 2. Bottom nav -> Log (tap-xy 848 2253). 3. `drive_android.py tree` -> note `View: Error [477,304][667,419]`. 4. `drive_android.py tap-xy 572 361` (centre of the Error chip). 5. `drive_android.py tree` again.
findings.evidence: a11y tree at step 3 and step 5 are identical for all four chips: `View: Info [32,304][208,419]` / `View: Warning [224,304][461,419]` / `View: Error [477,304][667,419]` / `View: Critical [683,304][904,419]` - no [ON]/[off] annotation on any of them, before or after the toggle. Screenshot /tmp/ns-android/shots/10-log-error-off.png taken after step 4 shows Error rendered grey-outline/grey-label while Info, Warning and Critical remain filled and colour-tinted, proving the tap did toggle real state. Source: apps/mobile/lib/screens/dashboard/tabs/log_tab.dart:367-432 - _SeverityChip returns InkWell -> Container whose only enabled/disabled difference is SkotiqDecorations.selectedSurface(...) vs a plain BoxDecoration, plus `color: enabled ? c : colors.textMuted` on the label; there is no Semantics node anywhere in the widget.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the Container in Semantics(selected: enabled, button: true, label: '${_severityLabel(severity)}${count > 0 ? ", $count events" : ""}'). The 44dp minHeight is already right; this is purely the missing state annotation.

findings.title: Every Settings toggle tears down the whole page to a spinner and throws the user back to the top of the list
findings.what_happened: Each of the 11 switches calls `await prefs.setX(value)` then `ref.invalidate(mobilePreferencesProvider)`. Invalidating that FutureProvider drops it back to AsyncLoading with no retained previous value, so `prefsAsync.when(...)` swaps the entire ListView for `Center(child: CircularProgressIndicator())`. The ListView element is destroyed and rebuilt fresh, so its scroll offset resets to zero. Observed: with the list scrolled to the bottom (Target completed at y=1807, Battery warnings at y=1998, Immersive Android mode scrolled off the top), I toggled Target completed - and the very next tree had Immersive Android mode back at y=433 with Target completed and Battery warnings gone off the bottom entirely. The list content is roughly 2,450px against a ~1,900px viewport, so the bottom three categories (Low disk space, Target completed, Battery warnings) always need a scroll to reach. Muting those three costs 3 swipes + 3 taps instead of 1 swipe + 3 taps, and each toggle flashes a full-page spinner that reads as the app reloading.
findings.expected: Toggling a switch should change that switch and nothing else. Hold the value locally (or use `prefsAsync.when(skipLoadingOnRefresh: true)` / a Notifier that emits the new state directly) so the list never unmounts and the scroll offset survives.
findings.repro: 1. Companion UI enabled; Skip Connection; bottom nav -> Settings (tap-xy 1003 2253). 2. `adb shell input swipe 540 1800 540 900 300` to reach the bottom of the list. 3. `drive_android.py tree` - confirm Target completed / Battery warnings are on screen and Immersive Android mode is not. 4. `drive_android.py tap 'Target completed'`. 5. `drive_android.py tree` again.
findings.evidence: Tree at step 3: `Switch: Target completed / Per-target completion alerts [ON] [42,1807][1038,1996]` and `Switch: Battery warnings / Low battery and power-protection alerts [off] [42,1998][1038,2187]`; no Immersive row present. Tree at step 5: `Switch: Immersive Android mode / Hide the status bar while monitoring a session [ON] [42,433][1038,622]`; neither Target completed nor Battery warnings appears in the dump. Same behaviour was seen earlier when toggling Battery warnings from a scrolled position. Source: apps/mobile/lib/screens/dashboard/tabs/settings_tab.dart:16 `final prefsAsync = ref.watch(mobilePreferencesProvider);`, :19 `prefsAsync.when(data: (prefs) => ListView(...)`, :160 `loading: () => const Center(child: CircularProgressIndicator())`, and the 11 onChanged handlers at :31-146 which each end in `ref.invalidate(mobilePreferencesProvider)`.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the FutureProvider+invalidate pattern with a Notifier that holds MobilePreferences and emits the updated snapshot after the write, so `when()` never re-enters loading. Cheapest local fix: keep a `bool` in _SwitchRowState seeded from widget.value and update it optimistically, dropping the invalidate entirely - the writes already go straight to SharedPreferences and each row is the only writer of its own key.

findings.title: Mount tab's empty state sends the user on an instruction that dead-ends, and never names the real blocker (no appliance paired)
findings.what_happened: With no appliance paired, the Mount tab renders 'Mount not connected / Connect the mount from the Devices tab to enable slew controls and tracking.' The gate is `state.connectionState != DeviceConnectionState.connected` - it never asks whether a HOST is reachable, so it emits the same device-level instruction whether the mount is merely idle on a connected rig or the phone has never spoken to a Skotiq server in its life. Following that instruction fails: the Devices tab's Camera/Mount/Focuser/Filter Wheel/Guider cards each render a full-width, primary-filled blue 'Connect' CTA, and tapping the Mount one produces the SnackBar 'No mount assigned in profile'. There is no profile because there is no host - the profile lives on the appliance the user has not paired with. So the user is routed from a wrong instruction to a second wrong explanation, and at no point is told 'this phone is not connected to a Skotiq server'.
findings.expected: Branch on host reachability first. When the backend is not a NetworkBackend, the Mount tab should say something like 'Not connected to a Skotiq server - pair with your rig to control the mount' with a button that opens the connection sheet, matching what SessionPickerScreen already does correctly ('Session replay requires the phone to be paired with a Skotiq server'). Reserve the 'Connect the mount from the Devices tab' copy for the case where a host IS connected and the mount specifically is offline.
findings.repro: 1. Companion UI enabled; Skip Connection (View UI Only) - no host ever contacted. 2. Bottom nav -> Mount (tap-xy 231 2253). 3. Read the empty state. 4. Follow it: bottom nav -> Devices (tap-xy 77 2253), tap the Mount card's Connect CTA.
findings.evidence: Tree at step 3: `View: Mount not connected [364,1198][716,1251]` / `View: Connect the mount from the Devices tab to enable slew controls and tracking. [68,1272][1013,1372]`. Screenshot /tmp/ns-android/shots/20-crop.png shows the Devices card CTA is a full-width primary-filled blue 'Connect' button, the most prominent control on that screen. Screenshot /tmp/ns-android/shots/30-after-connect.png, captured immediately after tapping it, shows the SnackBar 'No camera assigned in profile' (same code path for every device class). Source: apps/mobile/lib/screens/dashboard/tabs/mount_tab.dart:248-256 - `if (state.connectionState != DeviceConnectionState.connected) return const EmptyState(... 'Connect the mount from the Devices tab ...')`, with no backend/host check. apps/mobile/lib/screens/dashboard/tabs/devices_tab.dart:370-375 (camera) and :420-425 (mount) - `final id = profile?.cameraId; if (id == null || id.isEmpty) { _showProfileMissing(context, 'camera'); return; }`; :592-596 defines _showProfileMissing as the SnackBar 'No $deviceClass assigned in profile'. Contrast the correct pattern at apps/mobile/lib/screens/replay/session_picker_screen.dart:202 'Connect to a server'.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a `ref.watch(backendProvider) is! NetworkBackend` branch ahead of the device-state branch in mount_tab (and the other operating tabs), returning a 'not paired with a server' EmptyState with a button that opens the NetworkStatusIndicator sheet - that sheet already works and already offers Search for Servers.

findings.title: Session History's 'Refresh history' toolbar action is enabled while disconnected and produces no perceptible change, unlike every other dead action in the app
findings.what_happened: With no server paired, Session History correctly shows 'Connect to a server / Session replay requires the phone to be paired with a Skotiq server.' But the AppBar's 'Refresh history' button stays enabled. Tapping it runs _refresh -> _loadMore, which immediately hits `if (backend is! NetworkBackend)` and re-sets the same _LocalBackendNotSupported error, re-rendering an identical screen. No spinner, no SnackBar, no change of any kind. I tapped it and both the a11y tree and the screen were byte-identical before and after. The app disables dead controls correctly everywhere else on this dashboard - the Sequencer's Start and Stop both dump as [DISABLED], and the Log tab's 'Clear log' dumps as [DISABLED] - so this one enabled-but-inert action is inconsistent with the app's own established convention.
findings.expected: Disable the refresh action when the backend is not a NetworkBackend, exactly as Start/Stop/Clear log already do, so `tree` reports [DISABLED] and a gloved 2am tap does not go unanswered.
findings.repro: 1. Companion UI enabled; Skip Connection. 2. AppBar overflow 'More' -> 'Session history / replay'. 3. `drive_android.py tree` and note the screen. 4. `drive_android.py tap 'Refresh history'`. 5. `drive_android.py tree` again.
findings.evidence: Tree at steps 3 and 5 are identical: `Button: Back [11,139][137,265]` / `View: Session History [189,170][485,233]` / `Button: Refresh history [954,139][1080,265]` / `View: Connect to a server [380,1290][700,1343]` / `View: Session replay requires the phone to be paired with a Skotiq server. Replay reads from the server's database, not local-only state. [68,1364][1013,1513]`. The Refresh button carries no [DISABLED] marker in either dump. logcat showed no app-side output for the tap. Source: apps/mobile/lib/screens/replay/session_picker_screen.dart:183 `onPressed: _loading ? null : () => unawaited(_refresh())` - gated only on _loading, never on backend type; :60-71 _loadMore returns early on `backend is! NetworkBackend` after setting _error, producing no user-visible transition. Compare log_tab.dart 'Clear log' and sequencer_tab.dart Start/Stop, both of which dump as [DISABLED] in the same session.

findings.title: No single 'safe the rig' action: at 2am with clouds coming in, stopping the run and parking the mount are on two different tabs with no shared shortcut
findings.what_happened: The companion is the surface you hold when you are in bed and the sky turns. The two things you need in that moment - stop the sequence and park the mount - live in two separate bottom-tab destinations with no common entry point. Stopping means: Sequencer tab, then press-and-hold the Stop button. Parking means: switch to the Mount tab, then reach _ControlsRow, which is the FOURTH child of that tab's ListView (after _PositionCard, _SlewRateSelector and the _Dpad), so on a phone it is below the fold and needs a scroll first. That is a minimum of tab-switch + scroll + tap, with a tab switch in the middle, and nothing anywhere in the persistent chrome offers 'stop and park'. The AppBar has room - it currently carries only a battery percentage, a network dot and a 2-item overflow menu whose contents (Saved servers, Session history) are both cold-path.
findings.expected: A single persistent 'Safe the rig' affordance reachable from every tab - press-and-hold, destructive styling, one gesture - that stops the sequence and parks the mount in the correct order. Put it in the AppBar action slot or as a FAB. The press-and-hold pattern the Stop button already uses is the right interaction for this (it survives a pocket tap); it just needs to be reachable without first navigating to the right tab.
findings.repro: 1. Companion UI enabled; Skip Connection. 2. Note the AppBar actions on any tab: battery '100%' at [678,165][828,238] and 'More' at [954,139][1080,265]. 3. Open More: only 'Saved servers' [471,170][1059,296] and 'Session history / replay' [471,296][1059,422]. 4. Sequencer tab: the Stop control is `Button: Press and hold to stop the sequence / Stop [DISABLED] [551,2012][1038,2127]` - present only on this tab. 5. Mount tab with no mount: only the empty state renders.
findings.evidence: AppBar action inventory from the a11y tree on Devices/Mount/Sequencer/Log/Settings - identical on all five: `View: 100% [678,165][828,238]`, `Button: More [954,139][1080,265]`. Overflow contents from the tree after tapping More: exactly two items, Saved servers and Session history / replay. Sequencer Stop bounds and label as quoted, present on the Sequencer tab only. Source for the park control's depth: apps/mobile/lib/screens/dashboard/tabs/mount_tab.dart:258-279 builds the ListView as [_PositionCard, _SlewRateSelector, _Dpad, _ControlsRow, _SlewToTarget]; the Park/Unpark button is inside _ControlsRow at :805 `state.isParked ? 'Unpark' : 'Park'`. The below-the-fold claim is source-only - I could not measure its on-screen y with no mount connected, since mount_tab returns the EmptyState whenever connectionState != connected.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a third AppBar action - a red shield/park glyph - wired to a press-and-hold that calls sequencer stop then mount park, with a confirmation toast naming both outcomes. Failing that, promote Park into _PositionCard so it is above the fold on the Mount tab and costs one tab-switch plus one tap.

verified_correct: settings_tab: all 11 switches persist correctly across a full app restart. Set Immersive Android mode ON (from default off) and Sequence events, Safety and weather, Guiding lost and Battery warnings OFF, then `drive_android.py stop` + `start` + Skip Connection + Settings: every one of the five came back in the state I left it and the other six were still ON. Ground truth confirmed on disk via `run-as com.skotiq.mobile cat shared_prefs/*.xml`: flutter.mobile.androidImmersiveSticky=true, flutter.mobile.notify.sequence=false, flutter.mobile.notify.safety=false, flutter.mobile.notify.guiding=false, flutter.mobile.notify.battery=false.

settings_tab: no dead toggles. Every one of the ten mobile.notify.* preferences has at least one real runtime consumer - notifySequence via notification_service.dart:84 into enableSequenceNotifications (gating :448 and :481), notifyMeridianFlip at mobile_event_notifier.dart:325 and mobile_sequence_hooks.dart:478, notifySafety at mobile_event_notifier.dart:162, notifyGuiding :203, notifyExposureFailed :232/:407/:412/:423, notifyAutofocusFailed :301/:402, notifyEquipmentDisconnected :246, notifyDiskLow :343, notifyTargetCompleted :309, notifyBattery at power_service.dart:170.

settings_tab: the Immersive Android mode preference is re-applied at startup, not just at toggle time - main.dart:91 calls applyAndroidSystemUiPreference(immersiveSticky) during boot, so the setting does not silently lose effect after a restart. Toggling it live also produced the genuine Android 'Viewing full screen' system dialog, proving the call reaches the platform.
settings_tab: all 11 switches expose correct accessibility state - the a11y tree reports each as `Switch: <title> <subtitle> [ON]` or `[off]`, and the values tracked every toggle I made.
mount_tab: degrades without fabricating. With no host it renders only an empty state and exposes zero slew, tracking or park controls - no D-pad, no fake RA/Dec, no invented coordinates.

sequencer_tab: the run vitals are honest at rest - Frames 0/0, Elapsed 0m 00s, ETA em-dash rather than a fabricated number, target 'No target', state 'Idle'. Start and Stop both dump as [DISABLED]. The Stop control is a press-and-hold ('Press and hold to stop the sequence'), which is the right interaction for a pocketed phone.
sequencer_tab: the Load dialog degrades honestly - 'No saved sequences / Create one on the desktop and it will appear here.' with a working Close control.
log_tab: honest empty state ('Waiting for events / New events from devices, imaging, and the sequencer will appear here.') and 'Clear log' correctly dumps as [DISABLED] with nothing to clear.

session_picker_screen: the best disconnected empty state in the area - 'Connect to a server / Session replay requires the phone to be paired with a Skotiq server. Replay reads from the server's database, not local-only state.' It names the real blocker and explains why, which is exactly what mount_tab fails to do.

mobile_dashboard_screen: the AppBar network indicator is truthful and functional. Tapping it opens a sheet reading 'Connection Status / Not connected to a server / Network Type Wifi / Connected via WiFi' with a 'Search for Servers' button. I initially suspected that button was inert because neither the a11y tree nor a late screenshot changed - but capturing at 1.2s and 4.0s after the tap shows the label correctly switch to 'Searching...' and back to 'Search for Servers' by 7.0s, and the code path (network_status_indicator.dart:532-551) raises a 'No servers found on this network.' SnackBar. Not a defect.

mobile_dashboard_screen: tab state survives switching. The Log tab's severity filter and the Sequencer's expanded weather card both held their state across round trips to other tabs, consistent with the IndexedStack the screen documents at :38-42.
coverage_note:
Driven live on the ns_test_api35 emulator against the pre-installed debug APK (versionName 6.1.0), with no Skotiq host running anywhere - the disconnected first-run state was the subject, per the brief. Entry to the shell was 'Skip Connection (View UI Only)'.

HARNESS FINDING - the six units in this area are NOT reachable in the default build. Skipping connection lands in the shared SkotiqApp GoRouter shell (bottom nav Home/Gear/Imaging/Sequence/Guiding/Plan/More), not the companion dashboard. All seven companion tabs plus both replay screens sit behind isCompanionUiEnabled (companion_ui_config.dart:7-14). I reached them by exploiting the runtime half of that getter on a DEBUGGABLE build: `adb root; adb shell setprop wrap.com.skotiq.mobile SKOTIQ_COMPANION_UI=1`, then restart. The Android wrap.<package> mechanism runs the app under `sh -c '<value> exec app_process ...'`, which injects the env var that Platform.environment then reads. Any later agent needing these screens must repeat that. NOTE: I left adbd in root mode; run `adb unroot` and `adb shell setprop wrap.com.skotiq.mobile ''` to restore the emulator to its prior state. That same gate is finding 1 (P0): a release APK can never satisfy it.

HARNESS TRAP worth propagating - `uiautomator dump` does NOT capture Flutter SnackBars. I nearly filed a false P1 claiming the Devices tab's primary 'Connect' CTA was a dead control, because the a11y tree was byte-identical before and after the tap even on an immediate dump. An `adb exec-out screencap` taken in the same shell command as the tap showed the SnackBar 'No camera assigned in profile' plainly. Any transient Flutter feedback - SnackBars, toasts, brief button label changes - must be verified with a fast screencap, not with `tree`. The same trap almost produced a second false positive on 'Search for Servers'.

Coordinate trap: `drive_android.py shot` downscales to ~720px wide (cmd_shot passes -resize unless --raw), while a11y bounds and `input tap` are in the native 1080x2400 space. Crops computed from tree bounds must be scaled by 0.667, and tap targets read off a screenshot must be scaled back up by 1.5. Also, `tap` matches on the full concatenated node label, so `tap "Mount"` hit the Devices-tab device card rather than the bottom-nav destination - bottom-nav navigation in this shell needs tap-xy (Devices 77, Mount 231, Camera 386, Sequencer 540, Science 694, Log 848, Settings 1003, all at y 2253).

Not covered, and why: camera_tab, devices_tab and science_tab are in the same companion shell but are other agents' units - I drove devices_tab only far enough to test the instruction mount_tab hands the user. Everything behind a live host (slew controls, run vitals under load, the log tail against /api/logs/tail, replay playback) is untestable in a disconnected sweep by construction. No crash, ANR, overflow or layout error appeared in any tab; logcat showed no app-side exceptions across the whole session.
